content: Nizatidine is prescribed to treat and prevent the recurrence of ulcers. It is also used to manage conditions where the stomach produces excessive acid. Additionally, it is effective in treating or preventing occasional heartburn, acid indigestion, or sour stomach. This medication works by reducing the amount of acid produced in the stomach. Nizatidine is available both with and without a prescription. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Nizatidine is available in tablet and capsule forms, which are taken orally. It is typically taken once daily at bedtime or twice a day, with or without food. Follow the instructions on the package or your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take nizatidine exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it or take it more frequently than prescribed by your doctor. If symptoms of heartburn, acid indigestion, or sour stomach persist for more than two weeks while taking nizatidine, stop taking it and contact your doctor. Before taking nizatidine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to nizatidine or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially aspirin, antacids like Maalox or Mylanta, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had kidney or liver disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking nizatidine, contact your doctor immediately. If you forget to take a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Nizatidine may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if any of the following symptoms are severe or persistent: headache, dizziness, drowsiness, constipation, diarrhea, stomach pain, runny nose, sneezing, coughing, or sweating. If you experience any of the following severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately: skin rash, hives, itching, wheezing, or difficulty breathing. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in the container it came in, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature and away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or no longer needed medication properly. Consult your pharmacist about the correct disposal method. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Do not share your medication with anyone else. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
